display: Vancouver insurance broker who has placed liability cover for BC kayak, heli-ski, foraging and wildlife-tour outfitters for about twenty years.

signals.text: I'm in the middle of renewal season: forty-two adventure-tourism renewals between October and January, and I'm walking each client through what changed.
Underwriters are tightening wording for adventure operators this season, and I'm spending a lot of time explaining the new terms in plain language.
Foraging operators who include tasting now need a mycologist-verified identification protocol on file before we can even get a quote.
Operators with fifteen years of real experience and no formal paperwork are the hardest conversations right now. Underwriters don't know them, so I have to make their experience legible.
One underwriter has dropped night-paddling cover, and I'm looking for ways to help operators who run evening trips.
I'm hearing from underwriters that application questions are changing, for example food handling on wildlife tours, so I want to ask operators better questions at intake.
I read incident reports as a habit and want to keep learning how guide decision-making fails at the moment of choice, not just which rule was broken.
I'm planning my parents' 50th anniversary dinner for forty people in Kelowna on November 8, and the guest list keeps changing.
I'm halfway through a slideshow built from my father's scanned seventies slides and could use help with cleanup, captions or sequencing.
I'm recovering from knee surgery, about three months in and ahead of schedule, and I'm not travelling far until it's fully healed.
I run the cold-storage shelves at a Vancouver food bank on Saturdays and often need ways to move fresh produce fast.
I'd like more time away from desk work, but renewal season makes that hard until January.

offers.text: Placement of liability cover for guiding and outfitter businesses through six specialty underwriters.
Twenty years of reading incident reports. I can tell you which operators lose cover and what patterns underwriters react to.
I can draft risk-management protocols in the format and level of detail underwriters actually read.
I can explain what underwriters currently want on file and how long a renewal takes, for kayak, heli-ski, foraging, wildlife-viewing and rafting operations.
A network of guides, lodge owners and outfitters across BC and Alberta, which I can use to make introductions.
I can help an operator translate years of field experience into documents an underwriter will accept.
A home office in Kitsilano with a very good espresso machine, for coffee meetings with local operators.
Cold-storage handling and hand-repacking of donated produce at a food bank, plus a route into the Mount Pleasant volunteer group.

catchers.hypo: I run mushroom walks and I'm told I need a mycologist to sign off on my identification process. Where do I even start?
catchers.can: I can explain exactly what underwriters ask for in such a protocol, help structure the document, and introduce operators to a qualified mycologist if one reaches out through me.
catchers.confirm: Do you run guided foraging with tasting in BC and need your identification process signed off by a formally trained mycologist?

catchers.hypo: I'm a mycologist or botanist and I'm interested in certifying identification protocols for foraging guides. Is there demand?
catchers.can: There is demand right now. I can describe what underwriters need from a sign-off and connect the mycologist with BC foraging operators who need one.
catchers.confirm: Do you hold formal training in fungal or plant identification and are you willing to review and sign a guide's written identification protocol?

catchers.hypo: My underwriter dropped night paddling from my policy. Are there options?
catchers.can: I can check which of the six underwriters I work with still offer night-paddling terms and what documented procedures they require.
catchers.confirm: Do you run organised kayak or canoe trips in BC that happen partly after dark, and do you have written safety procedures for them?

catchers.hypo: I run wildlife-viewing tours with a packed lunch and my new application asks about food handling. How should I answer?
catchers.can: I can explain how underwriters now view food handling around wildlife and help the operator answer accurately, before the answers cause trouble later.
catchers.confirm: Do you run wildlife-viewing tours where food is carried, stored or served to guests?

catchers.hypo: My rafting or heli-ski guides are experienced, but I worry about their decision-making under pressure. What do insurers look for?
catchers.can: I can share, in general terms, the decision-making failures that appear in incident reports and help draft procedures that address them.
catchers.confirm: Are you looking to improve documented guide decision procedures rather than just buy cheaper cover?

catchers.hypo: I'm starting a small outfitter business in BC and don't know what insurance I'll need or what documents to prepare.
catchers.can: I can walk the new operator through what underwriters ask for in this sector and place cover when the safety documentation is in place.
catchers.confirm: Are you launching or have you recently launched a guided outdoor business in BC or Alberta?

catchers.hypo: I grow fruit in the Okanagan and have surplus at harvest. Do you know anyone who can take it?
catchers.can: I volunteer at a Mount Pleasant food bank in Vancouver that regularly receives orchard pallets, and I can pass on the contact.
catchers.confirm: Do you have surplus produce that could be delivered or collected in the Vancouver area?

catchers.hypo: I have a box of 1970s slides from my family and I don't know how to scan or care for them. My dad was a woodworking teacher who photographed everything.
catchers.can: My father is a 79-year-old retired shop teacher who shot most of our early family slides, and I'm digitising them now, so I can share what has worked.
catchers.confirm: Are you trying to digitise or organise a family slide collection from the 1960s or 70s?

catchers.hypo: I'm about to have knee surgery and I'm worried about getting back to normal mobility. Can anyone talk me through it?
catchers.can: I'm a few months out from a knee operation myself and can talk about the recovery from the patient's side, though I'm not a medical source.
catchers.confirm: Are you facing or recovering from knee surgery and looking for a peer conversation rather than medical advice?

forbids.text: I won't write cover for operators who skip documented risk procedures.
I'm not travelling far until my knee is fully recovered, so meetings are in Vancouver or by video call for now.
Saturdays are for the food bank, so I take no work calls then.
I don't discuss named clients' policies, premiums or claims history with anyone.

projects.name: Foraging-operator identification protocol
projects.text: A reusable approach for BC foraging and wild-edibles operators to meet the new underwriting requirement for mycologist-verified identification when tasting is part of the tour.
roles_needed: mycologist or formally trained species identifier

projects.name: Parents' 50th anniversary slideshow
projects.text: A slideshow for forty guests built from scanned family slides from the 1970s, for a dinner in Kelowna on November 8.
roles_needed: slide scan cleanup or colour restoration

policy.t1: When there's a real lead, I'll share the direction underwriters are moving, which documents they currently want, and typical renewal timelines. I'll also share a general view of how I could help, without naming any clients.
policy.t2: When the fit is clear and I know who you are, I'll talk about family events, my knee recovery, and the kinds of things I have seen go wrong with operators, in general terms.
policy.never: No named client's policy details, premiums or claims history, and nothing that identifies an insured business.
